company.title: Company view
company.text: You pay the contract value and receive a delivery system: vetted developer, SDM, quality gates and the 72-hour replacement standard. Every FCFA of your budget is accounted for publicly.

developer.title: Developer view
developer.text: 40% of every contract goes directly to you. This share is published and non-negotiable, so your income scales with the value you deliver, not with negotiation skill.

sdm.title: SDM view
sdm.text: Your share is tied to complexity: 8% on light loads, up to 12% on heavy ones. You earn more only when you take on more and deliver.

agent.title: Agent view
agent.text: Base share plus commission and a retention bonus. Acquisition and retention are rewarded, churn is not.

state.title: State view
state.text: The contract value stays in the regional economy: developer income, local partnerships, certification programs and reinvested reserves.

items.q: Is MRVIN100 a company or a model?
items.a: It is a published model: a framework of standards that companies, developers, states and institutions can adopt. The framework is open and documented here in full, and the standards are maintained publicly per market zone.

items.q: Why 40% of every contract for the developer?
items.a: Because the developer is the person who builds. The 40% share is the ethical core of the model, published and non-negotiable. It attracts and retains the talent that makes the whole channel reliable.

The model standardizes the framework, not a single price list. Percentages such as the 40% developer share and the 8 to 12% SDM range are fixed. Absolute prices are maintained per market zone: what is standard in Central Africa can differ from West Africa or Europe.

items.q: What is the Success Delivery Manager (SDM)?
items.a: Your single point of contact, responsible for coordination, sprint planning, weekly reports, escalation and quality gates. An SDM manages at most five projects at a time, so service quality is capped by design.

items.q: How does the 72-hour replacement standard work?
items.a: If a developer underperforms or becomes unavailable, a replacement profile is presented within 72 hours, with a paid knowledge-transfer overlap so the project never stalls. No negotiation, no extra invoice.

items.q: Can I start part-time and scale to full-time?
items.a: Yes. That is the standard path: start part-time (80h/month per developer) to validate the collaboration, then scale to full-time. Your developer, your SDM and your tooling stay identical.
